content.introduction: Federal Reserve officials signaled potential interest rate hikes if inflation stays high, contrary to expectations of rate cuts under new leadership. The Federal Open Market Committee maintained current rates but saw dissent, reflecting divisions among policymakers. This shift aligns with rising inflation concerns and a war-driven economic impact.

The readout of the most divided Fed policy meeting in a generation added critical detail about shifts in [two blocs](https://www.reuters.com/graphics/USA-ECONOMY/FED/gdpzajoegvw/) of Fed officials waiting to greet Warsh - a growing one wary of the inflation arising from the war in Iran and of any talk of future rate cuts, and a diminishing one still leaning toward lowering borrowing costs. The Federal Open Market Committee, the Fed's rate-setting body, left its short-term policy rate unchanged in a range of 3.50% to 3.75% last month, but [four policymakers dissented](https://www.reuters.com/business/fed-likely-hold-rates-steady-what-may-be-last-meeting-powell-era-2026-04-29/), the most since 1992. Meanwhile, a [Reuters poll](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-fed-avoid-cutting-rates-this-year-economists-still-say-war-driven-inflation-2026-05-19/) on Tuesday showed a hefty shift among economists away from previously solid expectations for rate cuts this year, with fewer than 50% now projecting a reduction by December, down from two-thirds just a month earlier. ## [World](https://www.reuters.com/world/). *   [Home](https://www.reuters.com/). *   [Home](https://www.reuters.com/). *   [World](https://www.reuters.com/world/). *   [Business](https://www.reuters.com/business/). *   [Markets](https://www.reuters.com/markets/). *   [](https://www.facebook.com/Reuters). *   [](https://www.instagram.com/Reuters).
